subject: FintechCo — Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Priya Singh <priya@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo — Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet you both on the demo this morning. As promised, a concise recap of the performance/SLO discussion and the suggested baseline SLA items so your infra and procurement teams can evaluate. Attached is a one-page SLO checklist and the load-profile CSV Rafael requested.

Quick summary of what we heard from you:
- Target latency (p95) for single-turn text generation: 150–250 ms (goal: 200 ms)
- Throughput: sustained 300 req/s, with periodic bursts up to 1,200 req/s for 2–5 minute windows
- Concurrent active users/sessions expected: ~800–1,200 (fan-out to many short requests)
- Streaming requirement: near-real-time token streaming for the UI (first-token latency prioritized)

Proposed Redwood SLO checklist (baseline):
- p95 response latency: <= 200 ms for requests <= 1k tokens (non-streaming)
- p99 first-token latency for streaming: <= 250 ms
- Sustained throughput: support 300 req/s with <5% error rate
- Burst capacity: ability to scale to 1,200 req/s for up to 5 minutes with graceful degradation and fallbacks
- Concurrency handling: autoscaling policy to maintain target latency at 1,200 concurrent requests
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency histograms, and live traces sent to your SRE team

Next steps / MAP (mutual action plan):
1) Rafael to review/load your sample traffic profile (attached) and confirm instance sizing + concurrency settings.
2) We’ll provision a short canary (48–72 hours) on a Dedicated pool to validate latency & throughput with your traffic.
3) Redwood to provide a canary report with p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, and cost estimate.
4) Procurement: draft terms for Dedicated capacity (if canary meets SLOs).

Attachments: 20260810-fintechco-slo-checklist.pdf (application/pdf), fintechco-load-profile.csv (text/csv)

Would love confirmation of the burst windows (daily/timezone) and the percent of streaming vs non-streaming requests so Rafael can size things appropriately.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist. A couple quick clarifications from our side before Rafael sizes things:

1) Tokens per request: our average prompt+response is ~600 tokens, 95th at ~1,400 tokens. Will that materially change the p95 target?
2) Streaming vs batch split: roughly 65% of user requests rely on streaming in the UI (incremental tokens), 35% are non-streaming backend calls.
3) Bursts: we see daily bursts aligned with US market open (09:30 ET) for ~10–12 minutes and occasional end-of-day batch spikes. The 1,200 req/s number is a high-water mark.

Also looping in Priya (procurement) — we’ll need an outline of the Dedicated commitment options and any trial credits for the canary.

—Alex

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks Alex — good context. A few technical notes and initial sizing assumptions based on the token distribution and streaming ratio you provided:

- Token impact: requests with ~600 tokens average are fine for our default execution path. The 95th at 1,400 tokens increases compute per request (~2–3x), which will push p95 up depending on batching. For strict p95<=200ms at 1,400 tokens we'd likely recommend a slightly relaxed p95 target for those tails or a dedicated high-CPU/gpu instance profile for those heavy requests.

- Streaming first-token latency: p99 first-token <= 250 ms is achievable if we prioritize streaming lanes and pre-warm KV cache for common prefixes. We generally measure first-token separately from full-response p95.

- Throughput & concurrency: to hit 300 sustained req/s with mixed token sizes we recommend an initial Dedicated pool config:
  * Baseline pool: 8 x A100-80GB equiv nodes (or equivalent Ampere gen) with autoscaling to 24 nodes for burst windows
  * Concurrency tuning: 512 active concurrent model contexts (we use async batching to keep latency low)
  * Expected steady p95 (600-token avg): ~140–180 ms in the baseline config; 95th heavy tails (1,400 tokens) ~220–400 ms depending on batching and cache hits

- Canary plan:
  1) Redwood will run a 72-hour canary using a traffic mirror of your profile (we can use the attached CSV)
  2) We’ll enable streaming-priority lanes and token-level tracing to capture first-token times
  3) Deliverable: canary report with p50/p95/p99 (first-token & end-to-end), error budget burn, and cost per 1M tokens

Action items for FintechCo:
- Please confirm percent of requests that include 1,400-token tails (approx %) and exact burst schedule for market open (local time).
- Provide any IP ranges for whitelist if you want a private VPC canary.

I’ll start drafting the instance-sizing doc and expected costs — Marissa, I’ll drop that into the Drive link and flag the key numbers for procurement.

-Rafael
